ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a circle with points M, N, O, and P on the circumference. Chords PM and PN meet at point P, forming the requested inscribed angle at P. The minor arc from M to N is labeled 70°. There is also a 56° angle marked at N, but it is not needed for this method. Reasoning: Angle P is an inscribed angle formed by chords PM and PN, so it intercepts arc MN. By the inscribed angle theorem, an inscribed angle equals half the measure of its intercepted arc. Therefore, m∠P = 70° ÷ 2 = 35°.
